author: tzhouam
body: This hunk is rebase alignment, although it doesn't look like it at first glance: `vllm_omni/benchmarks/patch/patch.py` is our patched copy of upstream `vllm/benchmarks/serve.py`, and upstream **v0.27.0 added the `probe_request_rate` probe loop to that file** (`serve.py:798,987,995` at the v0.27.0 tag; absent in 0.26). The change ports the new upstream feature into the patched copy so it stays in sync with its 0.27 base — dropping it would make the patched bench diverge from the file it patches. Added a provenance comment on the hunk in 24dbef7e.

author: tzhouam
body: The kwargs indirection is the version guard rather than a style choice: pre-0.27 vLLM's `init_model_parallel_group` doesn't accept `use_all2all`, so passing it as an explicit argument raises `TypeError` there. The `inspect.signature` check forwards it only when the running vLLM supports it (0.27's MoE oracle requires it; older vLLM has neither the kwarg nor the requirement). If you'd prefer it explicit, I can split into two literal calls — `init_model_parallel_group(..., use_all2all=True)` in the supported branch and the bare call otherwise — at the cost of duplicating the call site; or, if this branch is fine requiring vLLM ≥ 0.27, drop the guard and pass it explicitly everywhere. Which do you prefer?
